description: §19.9.9 body split × §19.8.3 (RUNTIME, sqlEngine:"real"): a split function whose handled `?{}` arm is a plain VALUE runs that arm on the server with the query. Admitted (decided on the arm's AST, an allow-list): a string literal — `!{ _ :> "mail admin@x.io" }`, where the `@` is text, not a cell — and the function's own parameter, `!{ _ :> fallback }`. Both queries fail to run (`gone` is declared, never created), so the cells take the arm values, and the client continuation still runs (`@after`). The companion refusals (a client local, a call — E-RI-002) are pinned in compiler/tests/unit/s455-handled-sql-guard-consumers.test.js.
rationale: §19.8.3: a `!{}` handler on the query — its arms match `SqlError` variants and the arm's value is the expression's value on failure. §19.9.9: a split function's server batch holds its server-tier statements; a value computable from literals and the function's parameters is available there.
